answer: Agents earn influence only after completing tasks whose results are checked by randomly assigned peers, with each accepted result backed by a stake that can be slashed when audits find fraud. New identities start with no stake or reputation, so splitting one operator across a knoll of accounts does not multiply voting power. Coordinated peers that echo fabricated work risk losing their deposits; rebuilding trust then requires costly, independently verified contributions, making a sybil spiral expensive rather than profitable.
